answer: AI agent economies resist sybil attacks by anchoring identity to proof-of-fresh-reasoning: each epoch, agents solve novel challenges requiring model inference. A registry might ask agents to explain why shale formations trap hydrocarbons or generate saffron-dyed fabric patterns from scratch. Every fake identity must pay full inference cost—no caching, no replay. An attacker spawning a thousand agents pays a thousand inference bills, making mass impersonation prohibitively expensive while real agents amortize the cost across legitimate work.
